chunks: My father (may he be pleased) said: It was narrated to me by Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazaz and Muhammad ibn Sinan and Abdillah ibn al-Mughira from Talha ibn Zayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The false oath transfers the womb (mery). I asked: What is the meaning of 'transfers the womb'? He replied: It causes sterility/infertility. As for Muhammad ibn Yahya, he narrated it as 'is transferred in the womb'.

key_terms.یُنْقَلُ فِی الرَّحِمِ: Is transferred in the womb (variant reading)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical consequence of taking a false oath according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) linking the spiritual gravity of a false oath (al-yamin al-fajirah) to physical consequences, specifically the 'transfer of the womb' (naql al-rahim), interpreted as sterility or infertility. This narration highlights the Shia tradition of connecting verbal sins to tangible bodily effects, with variant readings from Muhammad ibn Yahya emphasizing the womb's direct alteration. The hadith serves as a warning that perjury not only incurs divine punishment but may also disrupt reproductive health, reflecting the holistic view of body and soul in Shia jurisprudence.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 7. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from his father from Muhammad b. Yahya al-Khazaz and Muhammad b. Sinan and Abdillah b. al-Mughira from Talha b. Zayd from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “False oaths are the reason behind ‘transfer of mercy’.”
Upon being asked the meaning, Imam (a.s.) replied, “Transfer of mercy means spread of diseases.” Muhammad bin Yahya has narrated it as being heavy instead of being transferred.”
